reason: Conversation 2 did the one thing the ground truth marks as the sensible first step: it sent the homeowner (after telling them to unplug) to the front sump compartment, where they found and cleared slimy fluff and the dryer then ran noticeably longer, before correctly escalating to an engineer. Conversation 1 was honest, safe and never overclaimed, but it wrongly treated the sump as inaccessible on a stacked unit and jumped to 'book an engineer' without offering that front-access clean, so it left useful self-help on the table. Conversation 2 loses points for two wasted turns of irrelevant tests (drum warmth, a drain hose the customer had already said was not fitted), a possibly inaccurate 'white float lever' description, and a closing overclaim that it 'points strongly' to the pump needing replacement plus a parts panel when the truth is genuinely pump-versus-level-switch; those flaws keep the margin slight rather than clear.
